examples.ko: 그 작가는 서울에 있는 대학에서 명예박사 학위를 받았어요.
examples.en: That writer received an honorary doctorate from a university in Seoul.

examples.ko: 유명한 기업인이 우리 학교의 명예박사가 되었어요.
examples.en: A famous businessman became an honorary doctor of our school.

examples.ko: 명예박사 학위는 보통 사회에 큰 공을 세운 사람에게 줘요.
examples.en: An honorary doctorate is usually given to someone who has contributed greatly to society.
An honorary doctorate ceremony was also held at the graduation.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 명예박사 학위를 받고 매우 기뻐하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather was very happy to receive an honorary doctorate.

examples.ko: 명예박사로 선정된 분이 특별 강연을 해요.
examples.en: The person chosen as an honorary doctor will give a special lecture.

explain: 공부를 마쳐서 받는 학위가 아니라 대학이 업적을 인정해서 주는 학위예요. '명예박사 학위를 받다/수여하다'처럼 써요. 그냥 '박사'와는 달라서 '박사 과정'을 마친 사람과 구별해서 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 가수는 대학에서 명예박사 학위를 받았어요.
phrases.en: The singer received an honorary doctorate from a university.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명예박사'에 '학위'를 붙여 받는 사람 입장에서 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 학위 to the word is the most common way to say someone receives the degree.

phrases.example: 대학이 그 작가에게 명예박사 학위를 수여했어요.
phrases.en: The university conferred an honorary doctorate on the writer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽인 대학이나 기관을 주어로 할 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 공식적인 글에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the university or institution is the subject; common in news and formal writing.

phrases.example: 그 기업인은 올해 우리 학교의 명예박사가 되었어요.
phrases.en: The businessman became an honorary doctor of our school this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학위보다 사람 자체에 초점을 두고 '명예박사'라는 자격을 얻었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Focuses on the person gaining the title rather than on the degree itself.

explain_en: It is not a degree earned by finishing study, but one a university gives to recognize someone's achievements. It is used as '명예박사 학위를 받다/수여하다'. It is different from a plain '박사', so people keep it separate from someone who finished a doctoral program.

examples.en: I met a neighbor in the elevator and gave a light nod.
I nodded to my teacher in the hallway and walked on.

examples.ko: 처음 본 사람이라 목례만 하고 헤어졌어요.
examples.en: Since it was someone I'd just met, we only exchanged a nod and parted.
At a funeral hall, you nod silently to the bereaved family.

examples.ko: 눈이 마주치면 가볍게 목례할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If your eyes meet, you can give a light nod.

examples.ko: 직원이 웃으며 목례하면서 문을 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: The employee smiled, nodded, and opened the door for me.

explain: 말 없이 고개만 가볍게 숙이는 인사예요. 길게 말하기 어색한 자리나 잘 모르는 사람에게 많이 하고, '목례를 하다/나누다/건네다'처럼도 써요.

phrases.en: I met my teacher in the hallway and gave a light nod.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가볍게'를 앞에 붙여 고개를 살짝 숙이는 인사라는 뜻을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '가볍게' stresses that it is just a slight bow of the head.

phrases.en: Every morning I exchange nods with the man next door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 가볍게 인사할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when two people greet each other with a nod.

phrases.en: That person nodded to me first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람이 먼저 인사할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one person greets the other first.

explain_en: It is a greeting made by lightly lowering the head without speaking. It fits awkward moments or people you barely know, and it can also be used as '목례를 하다/나누다/건네다'.

examples.en: I went to pay my respects at my friend's father's funeral.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 선배 댁에 문상하려고 해요.
examples.en: I plan to go offer my condolences at my senior's house this evening.

examples.ko: 문상하고 나서 유족에게 위로의 말을 전했어요.
examples.en: After paying my respects, I offered words of comfort to the bereaved family.
Before going to the funeral, I got black clothes ready.

examples.ko: 바빠서 직접 문상하지 못해 마음이 무거워요.
examples.en: I was busy and couldn't go in person, so I feel heavy-hearted.
I paid my respects together with my coworkers.

explain: 장례식장에 가서 고인에게 인사하고 유족을 위로하는 일이에요. 말할 때는 '문상 가다'나 '조문하다'도 자주 쓰고, 뜻은 거의 같아요.

phrases.en: I'm going to pay my condolences at the funeral hall tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 자주 쓰는 형태이고 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form often used in speech, with the same meaning.

phrases.en: Many people offered their condolences.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같고 조금 더 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, a bit more formal.

phrases.en: Mourners keep coming.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장례식에 온 사람을 가리키는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for people who come to a funeral.

explain_en: It means going to a funeral to pay respects to the deceased and comfort the family. In speech '문상 가다' and '조문하다' are also common, and the meaning is nearly the same.

examples.en: Our choir's accompanist is a piano teacher.
The accompanist suddenly got sick, so the performance was postponed.

examples.ko: 반주자를 구하는 광고를 학교 게시판에서 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw an ad looking for an accompanist on the school bulletin board.

examples.ko: 노래할 때 반주자와 호흡을 맞추는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: When singing, it's important to be in sync with the accompanist.
I work as an accompanist at a church.
Please send the sheet music to the accompanist first.

explain: 노래나 춤 옆에서 피아노 같은 악기로 받쳐 주는 사람이에요. '반주를 하다'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요. 곡 전체를 혼자 연주하는 사람은 '독주자'라고 해서 달라요.

phrases.example: 친구가 제 노래에 맞춰 반주를 해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend played the accompaniment to my song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '반주자'가 하는 일을 말해요. 사람이 아니라 행동을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes what an accompanist does; it refers to the action, not the person.

phrases.en: The piano accompanist came to the practice room first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 악기로 반주하는지 앞에 붙여 구체적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put the instrument in front to say specifically what the accompanist plays.

phrases.example: 합창 대회 때문에 반주자를 구하고 있어요.
phrases.en: I'm looking for an accompanist for the choir contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공연이나 대회를 준비할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing when preparing for a performance or contest.

explain_en: This is the person who backs up a song or dance with an instrument such as a piano. It is useful to learn it together with '반주를 하다'. Someone who plays a whole piece alone is a '독주자' (soloist), so they differ.

en: passing away (honorific); death of an elder

examples.ko: 할아버지의 별세 소식에 가족이 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: The whole family gathered at the news of grandfather's passing.
Many people mourned that person's passing.

examples.ko: 신문에 유명한 작가의 별세 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article on the death of a famous writer appeared in the newspaper.
After hearing the news of the death, I went to the funeral hall.
The teacher's mother passed away yesterday.
My father passed away after a long illness.

explain: '별세'는 어른이나 존경하는 분의 죽음을 높여서 쓰는 한자어예요. 신문 기사나 부고에서는 '별세'를 쓰고, 가족끼리 말할 때는 '돌아가시다'를 더 많이 써요. 자기 자신이나 아랫사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The novelist passed away last week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기사나 부고에서 존경하는 분의 죽음을 말할 때 쓰는 동사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form used in articles and obituaries for a respected person's death.

phrases.en: I heard the news of his passing and went to the funeral hall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소식'과 함께 죽음을 전하는 말로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 'news' when announcing a death.

phrases.en: My grandmother passed away last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별세'보다 가족끼리 말할 때 더 많이 쓰는 높임말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite word used more often than 별세 when talking about family.

explain_en: 별세 is a respectful Sino-Korean word for the death of an elder or someone esteemed. Newspapers and obituaries use it, while family members more often say 돌아가시다. It is not used for yourself or for people younger than you.

examples.en: I heard your husband is coming today, Teacher.

examples.ko: 교수님과 부군을 모시고 저녁을 먹기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to have dinner with the professor and her husband.
I heard the president's husband is a famous doctor.
I hope your husband can come to the wedding too.

examples.ko: 집에 가시면 부군께 안부 좀 전해 주세요.
examples.en: When you get home, please give my regards to your husband.
Her husband works overseas, so she lives alone, I hear.

explain: 자기 남편은 '남편'이라고 하고, '부군'은 남의 남편을 높일 때만 써요. '남편분'보다 격식 있는 말이라 편지나 인사말에 어울려요. '부군께서', '부군께'처럼 높임 조사와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Your husband, teacher, arrived first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 남편이 주어일 때 높임 조사 '께서'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the honorific particle '께서' when someone else's husband is the subject.

phrases.en: Teacher, please give my regards to your husband.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 남편에게 인사나 말을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when passing greetings or words to someone else's husband.

phrases.en: What does your husband do, teacher?
phrases.nuance_ko: '부군'보다 덜 격식 있고 대화에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less formal than '부군' and more common in conversation.

explain_en: You call your own husband '남편'; '부군' is used only to honor someone else's husband. It is more formal than '남편분' and suits letters and greetings. It is often used with honorific particles, as in '부군께서' and '부군께'.

examples.en: The vice president is leading today's meeting.
He was promoted to vice president last year.
The vice president's secretary answered the phone.
When the president is away, the vice president decides.

examples.ko: 우리 회사 부사장은 해외 출장이 잦아요.
examples.en: Our company's vice president often goes on overseas trips.
I sent the report to the vice president first.

explain: '부사장'은 사장 바로 아래 직급이에요. 직급 뒤에 '님'을 붙여 '부사장님'이라고 불러요. 사장은 회사의 가장 높은 사람이고, 부사장 다음에는 보통 '전무', '상무' 순서로 내려가요.

phrases.en: I'll give this document to the vice president.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직급 뒤에 '님'을 붙여 존중하며 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '님' to the title makes it respectful.

phrases.en: A new person has taken the vice president position.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직급이 아니라 그 자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the position itself.

phrases.example: 그분은 십 년 만에 부사장이 되셨어요.
phrases.en: He became a vice president after ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 직급에 오른다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that someone rose to that rank.

explain_en: 부사장 is the rank right below the president. People add 님 and call them 부사장님. After 부사장 the ranks usually go down through 전무 and 상무.

examples.en: This Lunar New Year, we sent a gift to our in-laws' family.

examples.ko: 사돈댁에서 김치를 한 상자 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: Our in-laws' family sent us a box of kimchi.
Their home is far away, so we can't visit often.

examples.ko: 아들이 결혼한 뒤로 사돈댁과 가끔 식사해요.
examples.en: Since my son got married, we occasionally have a meal with his wife's family.
I went to pay my respects to the elders of the in-laws' family.

examples.ko: 우리 사돈댁은 부산에서 작은 식당을 하세요.
examples.en: Our in-laws run a small restaurant in Busan.

explain: 자녀의 결혼으로 가족이 된 상대 집안을 가리켜요. 며느리 쪽이든 사위 쪽이든 모두 '사돈댁'이라고 해요. 사람을 부를 때는 '사돈어른'처럼 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: The in-law families met and greeted each other warmly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집안 전체보다 상대 집안의 사람이나 관계를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the in-law relationship or person rather than the household.

phrases.en: My child's in-law asked after us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대 사돈을 높여서 부르거나 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A respectful way to address or refer to the other in-law.

phrases.en: Before the wedding, we went to pay our respects to the in-laws' home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 방문해서 예의를 차리는 상황에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a polite visit to the in-laws' home.
phrases.en_equiv: to pay respects to the in-laws' home

explain_en: It refers to the other family you became related to through your child's marriage, whether it is the daughter-in-law's side or the son-in-law's side. When addressing a person, people also say things like '사돈어른'.

examples.en: We held a farewell party for a senior who is leaving the company.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 떠나는 친구 송별회를 준비하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm preparing a farewell party for a friend who leaves next week.

examples.ko: 송별회에서 다 같이 편지를 읽어 줬어요.
examples.en: At the farewell party, we all read letters aloud.
I bought a handkerchief as a going-away present.
We said our goodbyes and parted at the airport.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁 송별회가 있어서 일찍 퇴근해요.
examples.en: There's a farewell party tonight, so I'm leaving work early.

explain: '송별'만 따로 말하기보다 '송별회', '송별 선물'처럼 붙여 써요. 떠나는 사람을 보내는 자리를 말하고, 반대로 새로 온 사람을 맞는 자리는 '환영회'라고 해요.

phrases.en: There is a farewell party on Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '송별'을 가장 자주 쓰는 형태로, 떠나는 사람을 위한 모임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, a gathering for someone leaving.

phrases.en: I chose a farewell gift for the teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떠나는 사람에게 주는 선물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gift given to someone who is leaving.

phrases.en: My friend said goodbye in tears.
phrases.nuance_ko: 떠나는 자리에서 하는 작별 인사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The goodbye said on the occasion of leaving.

explain_en: '송별' is rarely used alone and usually appears as '송별회' or '송별 선물'. It is for sending off someone who is leaving, and the opposite occasion, welcoming someone new, is '환영회'.

examples.en: My wife prepared dinner tonight.
I'll ask my wife and then give you an answer.
My wife is from Seoul.

examples.ko: 주말에 안사람과 같이 여행을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: I'm going on a trip with my wife this weekend.

examples.ko: 안사람이 요즘 일이 바빠서 늦게 와요.
examples.en: My wife is busy with work these days, so she comes home late.

examples.ko: 안사람 생일이라 오늘은 일찍 들어가 볼게요.
examples.en: It's my wife's birthday, so I'll head home early today.

explain: 남자가 다른 사람에게 자기 아내를 낮춰서 말할 때 써요. 남의 아내를 말할 때는 쓰지 않고 '부인', '사모님'을 써요. 요즘 젊은 사람들은 '아내', '와이프'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My wife is really good at cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 아내를 말할 때 '우리'를 붙이면 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'uri' sounds natural when speaking about your own wife.

phrases.en: I plan to travel with my wife this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '과'를 붙여 함께하는 사람으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 'gwa' to name the companion.

phrases.en: My wife is a teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안사람'보다 요즘 더 많이 쓰고 어디서나 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common today than 'ansaram' and natural in any setting.

explain_en: A man uses it humbly when speaking about his own wife to others. You don't use it for someone else's wife; say '부인' or '사모님' instead. These days younger people more often say '아내' or '와이프'.

examples.en: My daughter entered university this year.

examples.ko: 저희 여식이 늘 신세를 지고 있어요.
examples.en: My daughter is always indebted to you.
This child is my daughter.

examples.ko: 어르신 앞에서 여식 자랑을 해서 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I'm embarrassed to have bragged about my daughter in front of an elder.
I have one daughter, and she's a doctor now.

examples.ko: 여식을 먼 곳으로 보내는 마음이 복잡해요.
examples.en: I have mixed feelings about sending my daughter far away.

explain: 어른이나 윗사람에게 자기 딸을 낮추어 말하는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 남의 딸은 '따님'이라고 높이고, 평소에 가족끼리 말할 때는 그냥 '딸'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My daughter is getting married next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 딸을 낮추어 말하는 격식 있는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal, humble way to refer to your own daughter.

phrases.en: Teacher, please take good care of my daughter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 딸을 부탁할 때 쓰는 공손한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite phrase for asking someone senior to look after your daughter.
phrases.en_equiv: to ask someone to look after my daughter

phrases.en: Your daughter is very polite.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 딸을 높여 부르는 말이라 '여식'과 반대로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific for someone else's daughter, the opposite of '여식'.

explain_en: It is a formal, humble way to refer to your own daughter when speaking to an elder or superior. Someone else's daughter is honored as '따님', and in ordinary family talk people simply say '딸'.

examples.en: If there's something you don't know, ask your teacher.
I'd like to ask Grandmother how her health is.

examples.ko: 길을 모를 때는 어른께 여쭈어보면 친절하게 알려 주실 거예요.
examples.en: When you don't know the way, if you ask an adult, they'll kindly tell you.
I'll ask the department head first.
Asking the professor questions still makes me nervous.
I'm calling to ask about the schedule.

explain: '물어보다'의 높임말로, 선생님·어른·직장 상사처럼 윗사람에게 물을 때 써요. 말할 때는 '여쭤보다'로 줄여서 많이 말해요. 나를 낮추는 말이라 친구나 아랫사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: If you're curious about something, ask your teacher.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여쭈어보다'를 줄인 말로, 윗사람에게 물어보라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 여쭈어보다, used to tell someone to ask a superior.

phrases.en: I asked my grandfather for directions.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 물어본 일을 과거로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for having asked someone older or senior.

phrases.en: May I ask you one thing?
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문하기 전에 정중하게 허락을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask permission before asking a question.

explain_en: It is the honorific form of '물어보다', used when asking a teacher, an elder or a boss. In speech it is often shortened to '여쭤보다'. Because it humbles the speaker, don't use it toward friends or people younger than you.

examples.en: If there is something you don't know, ask your teacher.
I have to ask an unfamiliar adult for directions.
I asked my grandmother how her health was.
I'll ask my parents first and then decide.
Why don't you ask the professor by email?
May I ask just one more thing?

explain: '물어보다'의 높임말이고, 내가 윗사람에게 물을 때 '께 여쭤보다'로 써요. 윗사람이 물을 때는 '물어보시다'라고 해요. '여쭈다'도 같은 뜻이고, 활용은 '여쭤요/여쭤봐요'처럼 해요.

phrases.en: Teacher, may I ask one thing?
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 질문하기 전에 먼저 허락을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask permission before asking a question to a superior.

phrases.example: 여쭤보고 싶은 게 있어요. 시간 괜찮으세요?
phrases.en: There's something I'd like to ask you. Do you have time?
phrases.nuance_ko: 질문하고 싶은 마음을 공손하게 꺼낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite way to bring up that you have a question.

phrases.en: I asked my grandfather how he was doing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '여쭤보다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 짧아요. 윗사람에게만 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '여쭤보다' but shorter; only for superiors.

explain_en: It is the honorific form of '물어보다', used when you ask someone older or higher in status, as in '께 여쭤보다'. When that person asks, you say '물어보시다'. '여쭈다' means the same, and it conjugates as '여쭤요/여쭤봐요'.

en: to be aged; to be old

examples.en: My parents are getting on in years, so I worry a lot these days.
Even though my grandfather is advanced in age, he walks every day.
I gave up my seat on the subway to an elderly person.
The aged teacher came to school for the first time in a while.
My father-in-law is elderly, so he goes to the hospital often.
When you grow old, health matters most.

explain: 나이가 많은 분을 공손하게 말할 때 써서 '늙다'보다 부드러워요. 자기 자신이나 물건에는 쓰지 않고 '연로하시다'처럼 높여 말하는 경우가 많아요. 나이를 높여 말하는 '연세'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I visit my elderly parents often.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이 많은 분을 높여 부를 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form for respectfully referring to elderly people.

phrases.en: My grandmother is old, so she can't go far.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나이가 많은 것이 이유일 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used when old age is the reason for something.

phrases.en: That person is quite old, so he walks slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '연로하시다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 연로하시다 and more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is a polite way to talk about an elderly person and sounds gentler than '늙다'. You don't use it for yourself or for objects, and it is often raised to '연로하시다'. It is useful to learn together with '연세', the honorific for age.

en: chief director; chairman of the board of directors

examples.en: The chairman gave a congratulatory speech at the graduation.
The chairman of our school was a teacher long ago.
I made an appointment to meet the hospital chairman.
A new chairman will be chosen next month.
The staff passed on their thanks to the chairman.
The chairman's office is at the end of the third floor.

explain: 학교, 병원, 재단처럼 이사회가 있는 곳에서 쓰는 직함이에요. 회사 대표를 가리키는 '사장'과 달라요. 부를 때는 '이사장님'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: The chairman came to the school today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장'을 높여 부르거나 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The respectful way to address or refer to the chairman.

phrases.en: That person is the chairman of a scholarship foundation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장' 앞에 일하는 곳을 붙여서 어디의 이사장인지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the organization before the title says which body the chairman leads.

phrases.en: My uncle became the chairman of a hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이사장이 되다'로 그 자리에 오르는 일을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '이사장이 되다' describes taking up the post.

explain_en: It is a title used in places that have a board of directors, such as schools, hospitals, and foundations. It differs from '사장', which refers to a company head. When addressing the person, say '이사장님'.
